children: The rupee was on course for a more than 1% weekly fall on Friday as a sharp rise in oil prices heaped pressure on Indian markets even as central bank intervention limited the currency's decline.
Stocks and bonds in Mumbai fell, and the rupee
declined 0.3% to 95.70, weakening for the fourth straight day.

"The immediate support zone is now placed at 95.10–95.20. A sustained move above 95.50–95.80 could open the door towards 96.00–96.20 in the coming sessions," said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex.
Brent remained above $100 per barrel as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuelled fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies.
U.S. Treasury yields rose to multi-year highs, adding pressure on risk assets as investors price in more policy tightening from central banks across the globe.
Mounting global pressures have weighed on the rupee this week, eating away at an early-September rally that had lifted it to a two-month high of near 94.30 per dollar.
Dollar-rupee forward premiums nudged higher after the central bank likely conducted dollar-rupee sell/buy swaps for a third straight session.
Focus now turns to U.S. consumer inflation data for August, due later on Friday, which is expected to influence market expectations of U.S. policy rates.
India's inflation data is due on Monday, when markets will be closed for a public holiday.
fell 0.5% and the 10-year bond yield rose past 7% for the first time in three months.
